rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The previous sūrah's closing notice that what is near has drawn near is elaborated here as the nearness of the punishment hour.
rows.anchor: what is near has drawn near

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the previous sūrah uses the stars as evidence, this sūrah presents the moon splitting as evidence.
rows.anchor: the rising and setting of stars is presented as evidence over a claim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated refrain interrupts the arguments to challenge the stubborn audience to reflect on the truth established by sound proofs.
rows.anchor: Such repetitive verses in a sūrah occupy a special significance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The audience demanded a visible punishment sign to verify Qur’anic warnings, although the revealed Book was God's favor, able to teach, remind, and remove doubts.
rows.anchor: He revealed such a Book to them that had all the necessary features to comprehensively teach and remind them and remove their doubts.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is assured that the greatest signs will not make the obstinate believe because they follow desire rather than reason.
rows.anchor: The greatest of signs shall not induce them to accept faith because they do not follow sense and reason

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier nations' histories ought to teach the Quraysh, but they lack the capacity to learn from them.
rows.anchor: The anecdotes about the fate of various earlier nations should be a big lesson for them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should leave the deniers to the Judgment Day caller summoning them toward Hell; they will emerge from their graves like scattered locusts.
rows.anchor: They shall respond to his call, emerging from their graves like locusts scattered about

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's people, ʿĀd, Thamūd, Lot's people, and Pharaoh rejected their prophets as Quraysh do; Quraysh know their fate and will meet it if they follow suit.
rows.anchor: the people of Noah, (sws) the ‘ Ād, Thamūd, Lot (sws) and Pharaoh

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is a blessing that warns in advance and makes it easy for the Quraysh to take heed and remember.
rows.anchor: He has made it easy for them so they can seek a lesson from it and be reminded.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh are not an exception to God's past practice of not sparing disbelievers and should not imagine themselves an exalted breed.
rows.anchor: when in the past the Almighty has never spared the disbelievers, they should not consider themselves an exception to this rule.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers' imagined acquittal directive in heavenly scriptures or ability to defend themselves before God is foolish.
rows.anchor: written a directive of acquittal for them in the Hereafter in the heavenly scriptures

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will not treat disbelievers and the righteous alike: the former are punished in Hell and the latter rewarded with Paradise.
rows.anchor: never treat the disbelievers and the righteous equally

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sāʿah means the time of Judgment and punishment warned of throughout this sūrah group, especially through 53:57; it is near and calls for preparation.
rows.anchor: refers to the time of judgement and the punishment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers warn of both a worldly punishment for persistent denial and the Hereafter's punishment; the worldly seizure is the prelude to the final one.
rows.anchor: The only difference between the two punishments is that of the beginning and the end

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the two punishments form a prelude and culmination, al-sāʿah can include both; for each nation receiving a messenger its time has drawn near, so the statement is factual, not exaggerated.
rows.anchor: Viewed thus, the time of judgement has drawn near for every nation to whom a messenger is sent.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon's splitting is a sign of the approaching punishment; God specially manifests signs during messengers' times to establish their warnings and messengerhood, as 41:53 illustrates.
rows.anchor: in every nook and corner of this universe exist the signs of God’s power and wisdom

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon's splitting sign shows that the Qur’an's descriptions of cosmic upheaval are definite future events, with signs of their possibility already appearing in the world.
rows.anchor: these are definite occurrences which will happen one day

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger's signs need not be announced miracles or challenges, nor must people have requested that particular sign; it may appear to dispel their doubts.
rows.anchor: It is not necessary that a messenger present such signs as miracles; they can appear without any proclamation and without throwing any challenge.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Splitting the moon shows that no cosmic object, however immense, is immortal or independent: all are subject to God's command and can be destroyed.
rows.anchor: none of the objects of this universe, however huge it may be, is independent or immortal

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the author's view, the Qur’an and Hadith corroborate that the moon-splitting event occurred during the Prophet's lifetime; Hadith differ about its nature, not its occurrence.
rows.anchor: it is evident from the Qur’ ān and corroborated by Ḥadīth in my view that such an incident did take place.

rows.speaker: some earlier authorities and some people of these times
rows.claim: Some authorities read the verse as a future moon-splitting at Judgment Day, with past tense expressing certainty; the author rejects this as incompatible with context.
rows.anchor: Though this opinion is also ascribed to some earlier authorities and is held by some people of these times as well

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future-only reading disconnects the verse from 54:2, whose visible signs are dismissed as magic; at Judgment Day disbelievers cannot make that excuse and instead acknowledge the messengers' truths, as 53:8 says.
rows.anchor: if the verse is translated thus, it will bear no relationship with the next verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lack of wider historical reports does not disprove the event, since observation of such celestial events was limited to a local sphere in earlier times.
rows.anchor: had such an incident taken place, it should have been mentioned in the history of other nations

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier observers lacked today's worldwide observatories and communication, so reports were local; those local witnesses were reliable, giving no reason to deny the event.
rows.anchor: this sphere in itself belongs to reliable people; hence, there is no reason to deny the happening of such an event.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He considers it probable that future lunar research will find a portion detached from and joined to another part; lack of current scientific corroboration reflects science's limits, so one should wait.
rows.anchor: It is very probable that in coming times, scientists are able to investigate the moon in a more elaborate manner

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reassures the Prophet and rebukes deniers: their problem is unwillingness to accept reward and punishment, not lack of signs, and they would call an even greater sign magic.
rows.anchor: the real reason for their denial is not that they are not being shown a sign for numerous signs exist around them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mustamir describes the deniers' claim that the sign is familiar magic, continuously passed on by earlier magicians, and therefore not proof of the Prophet's extraordinary status.
rows.anchor: such magic has been shown and taught by magicians of the past which they have continuously transmitted to later generations of magicians.

rows.speaker: some people
rows.claim: Some interpret mustamir as “mortal,” but the author cannot find that sense in the Arabic literature known to him.
rows.anchor: Some people have interpreted the word
